verdict.rationale: React's own docs describe TypeScript support: adding @types/react and @types/react-dom gives "full React Web support" (react-docs-13). That supplies the type information an editor's TypeScript language service uses for completions and type errors, and the editor-setup page (react-docs-19) shows React documents editor tooling. However, the pack never explicitly describes autocompletion, inline type errors, or a React-specific language service integration. That outcome is only implied through the TypeScript tooling the product relies on. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of editor autocompletion and inline type-error behavior, any React-provided language service or editor plugin, and independent or hands-on corroboration of accuracy.
